devices.name: Anaphora
devices.definition: Repetition of a word or phrase at the beginning of successive clauses or sentences.
devices.example: We shall fight on the beaches, we shall fight on the landing grounds, we shall fight in the fields and in the streets, we shall fight in the hills.

devices.name: Epistrophe
devices.definition: Repetition of a word or phrase at the end of successive clauses or sentences.
devices.example: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I understood as a child, I thought as a child.

devices.name: Epizeuxis
devices.definition: Immediate repetition of a word for emphasis.
devices.example: Never, never, never give up.

devices.name: Diacope
devices.definition: Repetition of a word with one or more words in between.
devices.example: Bond. James Bond.

devices.name: Anadiplosis
devices.definition: Repetition of the last word of one clause at the beginning of the next.
devices.example: Fear leads to anger. Anger leads to hate. Hate leads to suffering.

devices.name: Symploce
devices.definition: Combination of anaphora and epistrophe, repeating words at both the beginning and end of successive clauses.
devices.example: Let us never negotiate out of fear. But let us never fear to negotiate.

devices.name: Polyptoton
devices.definition: Repetition of words derived from the same root but with different forms or endings.
devices.example: I have a dream that my four little children will one day live in a nation where they will not be judged by the color of their skin but by the content of their character.

devices.name: Alliteration
devices.definition: Repetition of the same consonant sound at the beginning of neighboring words.
devices.example: Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers.

devices.name: Assonance
devices.definition: Repetition of vowel sounds in neighboring words.
devices.example: The rain in Spain stays mainly in the plain.

devices.name: Consonance
devices.definition: Repetition of consonant sounds in neighboring words, not necessarily at the beginning.
devices.example: He struck a streak of bad luck.

devices.name: Sibilance
devices.definition: Repetition of 's' or 'sh' sounds to create a hissing effect.
devices.example: The silken, sad, uncertain rustling of each purple curtain.

devices.name: Onomatopoeia
devices.definition: Words that imitate the sounds they describe.
devices.example: The bees buzzed, the brook babbled, and the wind whispered.

devices.name: Tricolon
devices.definition: A series of three parallel words, phrases, or clauses.
devices.example: Veni, vidi, vici. (I came, I saw, I conquered.)

devices.name: Parallelism
devices.definition: Use of similar grammatical structures in successive phrases or clauses.
devices.example: Ask not what your country can do for you—ask what you can do for your country.

devices.name: Isocolon
devices.definition: Parallel structures of equal length, creating rhythm and balance.
devices.example: The bigger they are, the harder they fall.

devices.name: Polysyndeton
devices.definition: Deliberate use of many conjunctions in close succession.
devices.example: And the water, and the sky, and the trees, and the birds all seemed to rejoice.

devices.name: Asyndeton
devices.definition: Omission of conjunctions between parts of a sentence.
devices.example: I came, I saw, I conquered.

devices.name: Rhetorical Question
devices.definition: A question asked for effect or to make a point rather than to get an answer.
devices.example: If you prick us, do we not bleed? If you tickle us, do we not laugh?

devices.name: Exclamation
devices.definition: A sudden cry or remark expressing surprise, strong emotion, or pain.
devices.example: O Romeo, Romeo! Wherefore art thou Romeo?

devices.name: Ellipsis
devices.definition: Omission of words or trailing off to create suspense or imply something left unsaid.
devices.example: But I thought you said...

categories.name: Repetition Devices
categories.description: Devices that use repeated words, phrases, or structures for emphasis and rhythm

categories.name: Sound Devices
categories.description: Devices based on phonetic patterns and sounds that create auditory effects

categories.name: Structural Devices
categories.description: Devices that organize ideas in particular patterns for clarity and impact

categories.name: Emphasis Devices
categories.description: Devices that draw attention and create emotional impact through questions, exclamations, and pauses
